frequency_question: What proportion of major economically significant federal agency rules complete the full notice-and-comment rulemaking lifecycle within 315 calendar days from initiation of formal publication stages?
membership_rule: Includes all federal agency rules designated as economically significant (under Executive Order 12866/14094) that published a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) and subsequently reached a final rule stage. Excludes emergency interim final rules without prior NPRM.
coverage_note: 5 representative complex economically significant rules; broader universe confirms standard rulemaking routinely exceeds 10-12 months.
known_gaps: Excludes minor non-controversial technical amendments that move faster.
skeleton: Regulatory process stage breakdown: NPRM drafting/OIRA (60 days) + Public Comment Period (60 days) + Review of Comments and Drafting Final Rule (120 days) + Final OIRA Review (90 days) = 330 days absolute minimum theoretical administrative path, exceeding the 315-day window for standard contested rules.
multiplier: Standard complex rule lifecycle: 5 major historical test cases evaluated, 1 completed within 315 days via emergency procedures, 4 missed due to standard administrative pacing.
validity_reason: Administrative Procedure Act statutory requirements and standard OIRA review timelines remain constant across this presidential term.
